entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

content.text: Postgres and Redis both keep their data across restarts. Next: the evidence directory and a synthetic signed-token fixture (check 7). Both go under a git-ignored `.local/`.

input.command:
grep -qx '.local/' .gitignore || printf '.local/\n' >> .gitignore
mkdir -p .local/evidence .local/secrets .local/fixtures && chmod 700 .local/secrets
openssl rand -hex 32 > .local/secrets/token-signing.key && chmod 600 .local/secrets/token-signing.key
b64(){ openssl base64 -A | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='; }
H=$(printf '{"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}' | b64)
P=$(printf '{"sub":"user-synthetic-1","account_id":"acct-synthetic-a","iat":%d,"exp":%d}' $(date +%s) $(( $(date +%s)+86400 )) | b64)
S=$(printf '%s.%s' "$H" "$P" | openssl dgst -sha256 -mac HMAC -macopt hexkey:$(cat .local/secrets/token-signing.key) -binary | b64)
printf '%s.%s.%s\n' "$H" "$P" "$S" > .local/fixtures/token-acct-a.jwt
echo "token parts: $(awk -F. '{print NF}' .local/fixtures/token-acct-a.jwt)"; cut -d. -f2 .local/fixtures/token-acct-a.jwt | tr '_-' '/+' | base64 -D 2>/dev/null; echo
# verify signature round-trip
T=$(cat .local/fixtures/token-acct-a.jwt); V=$(printf '%s' "${T%.*}" | openssl dgst -sha256 -mac HMAC -macopt hexkey:$(cat .local/secrets/token-signing.key) -binary | b64); [ "$V" = "${T##*.}" ] && echo "signature verifies" || echo "SIGNATURE MISMATCH"
git check-ignore -v .local/secrets/token-signing.key; ls -la .local

questions.question: How should the flaky Go DB tests be fixed? (The db and handlers test packages reset and re-migrate the same database in parallel.)

options.label: Serialize DB tests (Recommended)
options.description: Run `go test -p 1 ./...` in CI and document it in the README. One-line change. Tests get a little slower, and the fix relies on a flag instead of the tests being isolated.

options.label: Database per package
options.description: Each test package creates and drops its own database (e.g. appdb_test_db, appdb_test_handlers). Truly isolated and safe in parallel, but it touches both test helpers and needs CREATEDB rights.

options.label: Advisory lock in helpers
options.description: Both helpers take pg_advisory_lock before the reset and migrate. The tests are still coupled through one shared database, and a lock only hides that.

options.label: Pin to what's installed
options.description: Node 22.13, pnpm 12.5, Go 1.22.5 in .tool-versions, engines, CI, and both Dockerfiles. Makes everything match today; Go stays one minor version behind.

options.label: Install the pinned versions
options.description: Keep Node 20.17, pnpm 9.11, Go 1.23.2. You install them (e.g. with asdf/mise), and I align CI and the Dockerfiles to Go 1.23.2.

options.label: Newest stable LTS
options.description: Move everything to current Node LTS, current pnpm, and current Go stable, and update all pins, CI, and Dockerfiles together.

options.label: Yes, branch + PR

options.label: Commit only, no push
options.description: Commit locally. You push and open the PR yourself.

content.text:
Step 0 (the preflight gate) **passes**. All 9 checks are recorded with the commands and their captured output in `workstation-preflight.md`, and CI is green on PR #1: https://github.com/paavik/webapp/pull/1. Both CI runs on the PR passed (`35903455290`, `35903678525`). The log shows Node 24.21.0 and Go 1.27.1 were used, and all 4 Go test packages passed. I haven't merged it.

**Problems found along the way:**
- **The web image didn't build.** With no `.dockerignore`, `COPY . .` copied your local `node_modules` into the image and broke it. The same gap was also sending `apps/api/.env` into the API build. I added a `.dockerignore` to each app, and now the stack builds and every service reports healthy. Ports answer on 127.0.0.1 and refuse connections from your LAN address.
- **CI on `main` was already failing** (run `35899612053`). The database tests and the handler tests both wipe and rebuild the same test database, and `go test` runs them at the same time. I couldn't reproduce the failure locally (0 in 35 runs), so this cause is inferred from the CI errors, not confirmed. As you chose, CI now runs them one after another (`go test -p 1`), and the READMEs and `CLAUDE.md` say the same. Two green runs don't prove an intermittent failure is gone; if it comes back, the stronger fix is a separate database per package.
- **Tool versions had drifted.** I moved everything to the current stable releases, checked against the official download sites: Node 24.21.0 LTS (installed with nvm and made the default), pnpm 12.6.0, and Go 1.27.1. The pins are updated in `.tool-versions`, `package.json`, `go.mod`, both Dockerfiles and CI. Your system Go is still 1.22.5; it downloads 1.27.1 automatically because `go.mod` asks for it.

Other changes:
- `scripts/record-versions.sh` now records all 15 required tools.
- The evidence folder, a synthetic signing key and a test login token are under `.local/`, which git ignores. The token format is a placeholder until Day 4/5.
- Redis was tested in a throwaway container and then removed. It joins Compose on Day 5.

**Still open (these don't block the gate):**
1. The assessor doesn't have read access to the repo yet.
2. Branch protection can't be turned on for a private repo on the free plan (GitHub returns HTTP 403). The options are making the repo public, upgrading the plan, or accepting that merges aren't enforced.
3. The repo has moved to `paavik/webapp`. Pushes warn about it; `git remote set-url origin git@github.com:paavik/webapp.git` fixes that.

After you review and merge PR #1, Day 1 starts in a **fresh** Claude Code session, so the day's transcript contains only Day 1 work. Before that session, you'll need a human peer for the interview and a separate reviewer for the blind check.
